mainTopic: Straining wine on שבת (its seriousness and its מלאכה) and the rules for setting up tents, canopies, beds and curtains on שבת
overview: The amud opens with אביי's new reason why חכמים forbid hanging a wine strainer on שבת: it is a rabbinic rule against acting the way one does on a weekday. אביי then sums up the rules for tent-like objects in three levels: some are פטור אבל אסור, permanent tents bring a חטאת, and items already prepared before שבת are מותר לכתחילה. Next the גמרא asks what happens if someone actually strained wine. רב כהנא says he brings a חטאת. רב ששת objects that a dispute cannot stretch from חטאת to רבי אליעזר's full permission. רב יוסף offers the עיר של זהב case as a precedent, but אביי shows that there רבי אליעזר was answering the middle view of the חכמים. The גמרא then asks which מלאכה straining falls under: רבה says בורר and רבי זירא says מרקד, and each explains his reasoning. The amud returns to temporary tents with רמי בר יחזקאל's ruling on a doubled cloak, followed by רב's three answers about a כילה and a מטה, which the גמרא reconciles as three different cases. It ends with רב יוסף's report about רב הונא's canopies and רבי חייא's ruling that a curtain may be put up and taken down, and a second teaching of רבי חייא begins that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: אביי's new reason: a rabbinic rule against weekday behavior
steps.stepSummary: After the earlier explanation was challenged, אביי says hanging a strainer is forbidden only מדרבנן, so that a person will not act on the holy day the way he acts on a weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: It is a rabbinic rule, so that a person will not act the way he acts on a weekday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier reason for why חכמים forbid hanging a strainer, and אביי gives a new one: it is a rabbinic rule against weekday-style activity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא tells us the earlier explanation did not hold up. אביי no longer links the ban to a Torah-level prohibition. He says חכמים simply did not want people doing ordinary weekday routines, like setting up a strainer, on a holy day.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; signals that a previous approach is dropped and a new one is offered
By rabbinic law, not Torah law
In the way he acts on a weekday
A regular weekday, not שבת or יום טוב

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
phrases.notes: 'Rather' signals that the previous explanation was rejected.

phrases.english: It is a rabbinic prohibition,
so that one will not act in the manner
phrases.notes: The reason behind the rabbinic decree.

phrases.english: that he acts during the week.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces an earlier explanation (on the previous amud) of why חכמים forbid hanging the strainer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the earlier reason with a new one: a rabbinic decree against weekday-like activity.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban on hanging a strainer was thought to come from a stronger, tent-related prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban is only מדרבנן, meant to keep the holy day different from a weekday.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hanging a strainer is a rabbinic prohibition against weekday-style activity.

steps.title: אביי's three-level summary of setting up tent-like objects
steps.stepSummary: אביי gathers the ברייתות into one teaching with three levels. Temporary tent-like items are rabbinically forbidden. Permanent tents bring a חטאת. Items already prepared before שבת may be opened לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי would gather the rules of the ברייתות and teach: A large wineskin, a strainer, a bed canopy, and a folding chair whose cover comes apart: one should not set them up, but if he did, he is exempt from a חטאת, though it is forbidden. Permanent tents: one should not make them, and if he did, he must bring a חטאת. But a bed, a folding chair whose cover stays attached, and a folding toilet may be opened even לכתחילה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי organizes all the rules about setting up tent-like objects on שבת into one clear list with three levels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Level one covers temporary tent-like setups. Doing them is forbidden מדרבנן, but there is no חטאת. Level two covers permanent tents. Making one is real Torah-level building and brings a חטאת. Level three covers items that are already built and just need to be opened, so they are fully permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: The rules (literally 'the stringencies') of the ברייתות
Exempt from punishment, but still forbidden (a rabbinic level)
Must bring a sin-offering; this means a Torah-level violation done by mistake
To open or set them up even from the start, with full permission

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels: temporary tent-like items are פטור אבל אסור, a permanent tent brings a חטאת, and pre-built folding items are מותר לכתחילה.
steps.confusionAlert: There are two kinds of folding chair here. A כסא גלין has a cover that comes off, so setting it up is like making a tent and is forbidden. A כסא טרסקל has a cover that stays attached, so opening it is permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This three-level scale is a classic framework for the laws of making an אוהל on שבת.

phrases.english: Abaye would gather the principles of the baraitot and teach:
A large wineskin and a strainer,
a bed canopy and a folding chair (with a detachable cover) —
one may not set them up,
and if he did — he is exempt, but it is forbidden.
Permanent tents — one may not make them,
and if he did — he is liable to bring a sin-offering.
But a bed, a folding chair (with an attached cover), and a folding toilet —
it is permitted to open them from the outset.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 1 by placing the strainer within a full scale of tent-related rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Temporary tent-like setups are rabbinically forbidden, permanent tents bring a חטאת, and pre-built folding items are permitted לכתחילה.

steps.title: What if someone actually strained wine on Shabbat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that one may not pour wine into a hanging strainer on שבת. It then asks: if someone did strain wine, what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And one may not pour wine into a hanging strainer on שבת.' A question was asked: If someone strained, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks how serious it is if a person actually strained wine on שבת. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says straining is not allowed. It does not say how serious a violation it is. The question is whether straining is a full Torah-level מלאכה that brings a חטאת or something lighter.

keyTerms.meaning: A strainer that is already hanging
A question was asked before them (the חכמים)

phrases.english: 'And one may not pour into a hanging strainer on Shabbat.'
phrases.notes: A quote of the חכמים' opinion in the משנה.

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
If one strained, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from hanging the strainer to the act of straining itself, as the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is someone who strained wine on שבת liable to bring a חטאת, or is it a lesser violation?

steps.title: רב כהנא: straining brings a sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא rules that someone who strained wine on שבת must bring a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: If someone strained, he must bring a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers the question: straining wine on שבת is a full Torah-level violation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being חייב חטאת means this is a real Torah מלאכה, not just a rabbinic rule. Which מלאכה straining falls under is debated later (steps 9-12): רבה says בורר and רבי זירא says מרקד.

keyTerms.meaning: Must bring a sin-offering; here it shows רב כהנא treats straining as a Torah-level מלאכה

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
If one strained — he is liable to bring a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Straining wine on שבת makes one liable to bring a חטאת.

steps.title: רב ששת: the gap between the opinions is too big
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת attacks רב כהנא's answer. It makes no sense that חכמים would require a חטאת for something that רבי אליעזר allows even לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objected: Is there anything for which חכמים require a חטאת, yet רבי אליעזר allows it from the start?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת challenges רב כהנא. If straining brings a חטאת, the two opinions in the משנה would be impossibly far apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אליעזר allows pouring wine into a hanging strainer on שבת. If חכמים held this is a full Torah-level מלאכה, the two sides would range from fully permitted to Torah-level liability. Such an extreme split within one משנה is unlikely, so רב כהנא's ruling seems wrong. In the next step רב יוסף pushes back against this objection, and in step 8 אביי rejects רב יוסף's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there anything at all? (a rhetorical challenge)

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet strongly objects to this:
Is there anything
for which the Rabbis impose a sin-offering,
and Rabbi Eliezer permits it from the outset?!
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question that works as a challenge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב כהנא's answer in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's ruling that straining brings a חטאת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If his ruling were true, the משנה's dispute would stretch from fully permitted (רבי אליעזר) to Torah-level חטאת (חכמים), which is an unreasonably large gap.

steps.title: רב יוסף points to a case with the same wide gap
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges רב ששת's objection. In the case of עיר של זהב, רבי מאיר requires a חטאת and רבי אליעזר permits it לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: Why can't that happen? Look at the case of the 'city of gold' ornament. רבי מאיר says she must bring a חטאת, and רבי אליעזר allows it even from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף pushes back against רב ששת. He says a dispute can stretch from 'חטאת' all the way to 'allowed לכתחילה', and he gives a real example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת said that a gap from חטאת to מותר לכתחילה is impossible. רב יוסף answers with a precedent where exactly that gap seems to exist. If he is right, רב כהנא's ruling of חטאת could stand.

keyTerms.meaning: 'City of gold': a gold ornament shaped like Jerusalem, worn by women

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not attacking רב כהנא. He is attacking רב ששת's attack, which means he is defending רב כהנא.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef strongly objected to it:
Why not?
Look at the 'city of gold' ornament,
where Rabbi Meir requires a sin-offering,
phrases.notes: He holds that wearing it into a public domain counts as carrying.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Eliezer permits it even from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יוֹסֵף: אַלְּמָה לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counter-attack on רב ששת's objection in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that a dispute cannot range from חטאת to מותר לכתחילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known dispute already shows exactly that range, so the claim is false.

steps.title: The ברייתא behind the city of gold dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא. רבי מאיר says she is liable to a חטאת. חכמים say she may not go out with it but is exempt if she did. רבי אליעזר says she may go out with it לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is that case? A ברייתא teaches: A woman may not go out wearing a city of gold. If she did go out, she must bring a חטאת. This is the view of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say she should not go out, but if she did, she is exempt. רבי אליעזר says a woman may go out wearing a city of gold even from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fills in the source for רב יוסף's example by quoting the full ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא actually has three views, not two. רבי מאיר says חטאת, the חכמים say forbidden but no חטאת, and רבי אליעזר says fully allowed. That middle view will be the key to אביי's answer.

phrases.english: What is it? As it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא תֵּצֵא אִשָּׁה בְּעִיר שֶׁל זָהָב,
phrases.english: A woman may not go out with a city of gold,
and if she went out, she is liable to a sin-offering;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say: She may not go out,
but if she went out, she is exempt.
Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹצְאָה אִשָּׁה בְּעִיר שֶׁל זָהָב לְכַתְּחִילָּה.
phrases.english: A woman may go out with a city of gold from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source text for רב יוסף's example
steps.raayaObject: That a dispute can range from חטאת to מותר לכתחילה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of עיר של זהב (רבי מאיר, חכמים, רבי אליעזר)

steps.title: אביי: רבי אליעזר was answering the middle view
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רב יוסף's proof. רבי אליעזר was not responding to רבי מאיר's חטאת. He was responding to the חכמים, who said פטור אבל אסור, and he told them it is fully permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Do you think רבי אליעזר is arguing against רבי מאיר, who said she must bring a חטאת? No. He is arguing against the חכמים, who said she is exempt but it is forbidden. He told them: it is permitted even from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי knocks down רב יוסף's proof. He shows that in the ברייתא, רבי אליעזר's argument is only one step away from the view he is answering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each opinion in the ברייתא argues with the view next to it. רבי אליעזר argues with the חכמים, and the חכמים argue with רבי מאיר. Nobody jumps straight from חטאת to מותר לכתחילה. So the proof fails, and רב ששת's objection against רב כהנא still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Is standing on, meaning is responding to
Exempt from punishment, but still forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: A dispute is measured against the opinion it is actually answering. In a three-way argument, the two outer opinions do not prove that a direct חטאת-versus-מותר dispute is possible.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps רב ששת's rule in place. That makes it hard to say the חכמים of our משנה require a חטאת for straining when רבי אליעזר permits it.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מִי סָבְרַתְּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אַדְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר קָאֵי,
phrases.english: Do you think Rabbi Eliezer is responding to Rabbi Meir,
who said she is liable to a sin-offering?
He is responding to the Rabbis,
who say one is exempt but it is forbidden,
and he told them that it is permitted from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the ברייתא quoted in step 7
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב יוסף assumed רבי אליעזר was answering רבי מאיר. In fact he was answering the middle view of the חכמים.

steps.title: Which מלאכה is involved in straining?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: when someone strains on שבת, under which מלאכה do we give him a warning?
steps.simpleTranslation: Under which forbidden labor do we warn him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about straining. It wants to know which of the מלאכות straining belongs to. This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Punishment requires a warning (התראה) that names the specific forbidden act. So the גמרא needs to know which category of מלאכה straining falls under.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of what? Under which category?

phrases.english: Under which labor do we warn him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב כהנא's ruling in step 4 that straining brings a חטאת, and asks which מלאכה that liability falls under, despite רב ששת's objection.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The מלאכה category of straining, which is needed for a proper התראה

steps.title: Selecting or sifting
steps.stepSummary: רבה says straining falls under בורר. רבי זירא says it falls under מרקד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: because of selecting. רבי זירא said: because of sifting.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question. Each one places straining under a different מלאכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה sees straining as separating the good wine from the waste, which is בורר. רבי זירא compares it to pushing flour through a sieve, which is מרקד. Both views treat straining as a real מלאכה. They only disagree about its category.

keyTerms.meaning: Sifting, as with flour in a sieve

phrases.english: Rabba said: because of selecting.
Rabbi Zeira said: because of sifting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9

steps.title: רבה explains why straining is like selecting
steps.stepSummary: רבה supports his view that straining is בורר: in both cases, the good part is separated and the waste is left behind.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: My view makes sense. How does a person who selects work? He takes the food and leaves the waste. Here too, when straining, he takes the food and leaves the waste.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives his reason for calling straining בורר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בורר, a person separates good food from waste. When wine passes through a strainer, the good wine is also separated from the dregs, which stay behind. To רבה, the result is the same, so the מלאכה is the same.

keyTerms.meaning: My own view is the logical one

phrases.english: Rabba said: According to my view it is reasonable:
What is the way of one who selects?
He takes food and leaves the refuse,
here too, likewise:

phrases.aramaic: נוֹטֵל אֶת הָאוֹכֵל וּמַנִּיחַ אֶת הַפְּסוֹלֶת.
phrases.english: he takes the food and leaves the refuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for רבה's answer in step 10.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: straining matches how בורר works (good part separated, waste left)

steps.title: רבי זירא explains why straining is like sifting
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא supports his view that straining is מרקד: in both, the waste stays on top and the food falls below.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: My view makes sense. How does sifting work? The waste stays on top and the food goes below. Here too, the waste stays on top and the food goes below.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives his reason for calling straining מרקד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא looks at how the separation happens, not only at the result. A sieve keeps the waste on top while the good part falls through, and a strainer does exactly the same. So straining matches מרקד more closely than plain בורר.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה looks at the result (good separated from bad), so straining is בורר. רבי זירא looks at the method (waste on top, food falling through), so straining is מרקד.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא, כְּווֹתִי דִּידִי מִסְתַּבְּרָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: According to my view it is reasonable:
What is the way of sifting?
Refuse is on top and food is below,
here too, likewise:
refuse is on top and food is below.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא, כְּווֹתִי דִּידִי מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's reasoning with a parallel argument for the other side.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: straining matches how a sieve works (waste on top, food below)

steps.title: A doubled cloak as a temporary tent
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one should not make a tent-like covering from a doubled טלית on שבת. If it was already tied with a string before שבת, spreading it is fully permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר יחזקאל taught: One may not make a doubled cloak into a covering. If he did, he is exempt but it is forbidden. If a string or cord was wrapped around it, he may spread it out from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the topic of temporary tents (אהל) on שבת, which it already discussed in אביי's list in step 2. Here it brings a ברייתא about a folded cloak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Draping a cloak over a rope to make a covering is like building a temporary tent. Doing it is a rabbinic איסור only, so he brings no חטאת. If the string was already attached before שבת, the tent was partly set up beforehand, so spreading it is not considered making something new.

keyTerms.meaning: To stretch it out, to spread it

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic rule for temporary tents: if the setup was done before שבת, spreading it out on שבת can be allowed.

phrases.english: Rami bar Yechezkel taught:
A doubled cloak, one may not make it (into a covering),
and if he made it, he is exempt but it is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה כָּרוּךְ עָלֶיהָ חוּט אוֹ מְשִׁיחָה —
phrases.english: If a string or cord was wrapped around it,
it is permitted to stretch it out from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from straining to the topic of temporary tents.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Making a doubled טלית into a covering is פטור אבל אסור. If a string was attached before שבת, it is permitted לכתחילה.

steps.title: רב כהנא asks about a canopy
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא asks רב whether one may set up a כילה on שבת. רב answers that even a מטה is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא asked רב: What is the law of a canopy? He said to him: Even a bed is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא asks a question, and רב gives a surprising answer that seems to make the case even stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב does not just say the כילה is forbidden. He says "even a מטה is forbidden," so a canopy is surely forbidden. This answer will soon seem to clash with his next answers.

keyTerms.meaning: A canopy, a tent-like net over a bed
A bed (step 17 explains which kind of bed each answer means)

phrases.english: Rav Kahana asked of Rav:
A canopy, what is the law?
He said to him: Even a bed is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the temporary-tent topic with a new question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May one set up a canopy on שבת?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even a bed is forbidden, so certainly a canopy.

steps.title: רב כהנא asks about a bed
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא asks about a מטה. רב answers that even a כילה is permitted, which seems to contradict his first answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law of a bed? He said to him: Even a canopy is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא asks a second question, and רב's answer now points the other way, toward leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, רב said even a bed is forbidden. Now he says even a canopy is permitted. Both answers cannot apply to the same kind of case, so they must be talking about different situations.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב changed his mind. Each answer refers to a different kind of כילה or מטה, and the גמרא explains the difference in step 17.

phrases.english: A bed, what is the law?
He said to him: Even a canopy is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second question whose answer seems to contradict step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May one set up a bed on שבת?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even a canopy is permitted, so certainly a bed.

steps.title: רב כהנא asks about a canopy and a bed together
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא asks about a כילה and a מטה together. רב answers that the כילה is forbidden and the מטה is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law of a canopy and a bed? He said to him: A canopy is forbidden and a bed is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: In his third question, רב כהנא asks about both items together, and רב separates them. This sets up the גמרא's next step: explaining how רב's three answers fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רב treats the two items differently: the canopy is forbidden and the bed is permitted. This is a third position, different from both earlier answers. The גמרא will need to explain which kind of canopy and bed each answer is about.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's three answers: (1) even a bed is forbidden, (2) even a canopy is permitted, (3) canopy forbidden, bed permitted. They look contradictory, and the גמרא will resolve them next.

phrases.english: A canopy and a bed, what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כִּילָּה אֲסוּרָה וּמִטָּה מוּתֶּרֶת.
phrases.english: He said to him: A canopy is forbidden and a bed is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third question, completing a set of answers that seem to contradict each other.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the law when both a canopy and a bed are involved?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The canopy is forbidden and the bed is permitted.

steps.title: רב's three answers were about three different cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב's answers do not contradict each other. Each answer refers to a different type of bed or canopy.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no contradiction. When רב said 'even a bed is forbidden,' he meant folding beds like those of the קרמנאי. When he said 'even a canopy is permitted,' he meant a canopy prepared the way רמי בר יחזקאל taught. When he said 'a canopy is forbidden and a bed is permitted,' he meant ordinary beds and canopies like ours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Steps 14-16: why did רב give three different answers? Each answer was about a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A folding bed of the קרמנאי opens up like a tent, so even a bed can be forbidden. A canopy that was already tied with a string before שבת, as רמי בר יחזקאל taught, may be spread. With our normal beds, which don't fold, setting up the bed is fine, but spreading a canopy is like making a tent, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
The קרמנאי, a people whose beds folded open like a tent
The sage (step 13) who taught that a doubled טלית with a string wrapped around it before שבת may be spread; the גמרא applies his ruling to a canopy
Like ours, meaning ordinary local beds and canopies

steps.whatToRemember: The same object can be permitted or forbidden depending on how it is built. A folding bed is like a tent. A canopy prepared before שבת may be spread. An ordinary canopy is forbidden, but an ordinary bed is fine.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב changed his mind or contradicted himself. He was simply answering about three different kinds of objects.

phrases.english: And it is not difficult.
That which he said, 'even a bed is forbidden' —
refers to beds like those of the Carmanians.
phrases.notes: These were folding beds that opened up like a tent.

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּקָאֲמַר לֵיהּ אַף כִּילָּה מוּתֶּרֶת —
phrases.english: That which he told him, 'even a canopy is permitted' —
refers to the case of Rami bar Yechezkel.
phrases.notes: The canopy was tied with a string before שבת.

phrases.english: 'A canopy is forbidden and a bed is permitted' —
refers to beds and canopies like ours.
phrases.notes: Ordinary beds that do not fold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the apparent contradiction between רב's answers in Steps 14-16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: אוקימתא: each answer refers to a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's answers seemed to contradict each other about the כילה and the מטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Folding bed = forbidden; canopy prepared before שבת = permitted; ordinary canopy = forbidden, ordinary bed = permitted.

steps.title: רב יוסף saw רב הונא's canopies spread and taken down
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף reports that in רב הונא's house the canopies were spread out in the evening and lying on the ground in the morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: I saw the canopies of רב הונא's house. In the evening they were spread out, and in the morning they were taken down and lying on the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a real-life observation of how canopies were handled in רב הונא's home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seeing the canopies spread at night and taken down in the morning shows that, in a proper case, a canopy may be put up and taken down on שבת. This matches the idea that a prepared canopy, as in רמי בר יחזקאל's case, is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Cast down and lying on the ground

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: חֲזֵינָא לְהוּ לְכִילֵּי דְּבֵי רַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: I saw the canopies of the house of Rav Huna
that in the evening were spread out
and in the morning were cast off and lying on the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical example showing that canopies can be spread and taken down on שבת.
steps.raayaObject: That a canopy may be spread and taken down on שבת in a proper case.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יוסף's own observation of the practice in רב הונא's house.

steps.title: A curtain may be spread and taken down
steps.stepSummary: רב, quoting רבי חייא, rules that a curtain may be both spread out and taken down on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said in the name of רבי חייא: A curtain may be spread out, and it may be taken down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about a curtain (וילון), which hangs like a wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A curtain has no roof, so spreading it is not like making a tent. That is why both putting it up and taking it down are permitted, unlike an ordinary canopy.

keyTerms.meaning: A hanging curtain, with no roof
A great sage at the end of the period of the תנאים

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the problem is a roof-like covering (אהל). A side wall alone, like a curtain, is not a problem.

phrases.english: Rav said in the name of Rabbi Chiyya:
A curtain, it is permitted to spread it
and it is permitted to take it down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from canopies to a related object, a curtain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A curtain may be spread and taken down on שבת, because it has no roof.

steps.title: שמואל's teaching in the name of רבי חייא begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces another teaching of רבי חייא, this time quoted by שמואל. The content continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said in the name of רבי חייא:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. It introduces שמואל's version of רבי חייא's teaching, which comes right on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא is about to give a second ruling from רבי חייא, quoted by a different student. This one will likely add to or parallel רב's ruling about the curtain.

keyTerms.meaning: A leading אמורא of בבל, a colleague of רב

phrases.english: And Shmuel said in the name of Rabbi Chiyya:
phrases.notes: The statement itself continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a second teaching of רבי חייא that parallels the one in Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet given on this amud; this line only introduces the statement.
